findings.claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T must be honoured, but without a surrogate the collector ignores every attribute on T. It always calls CreateContractlessMembers, which never reads [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract], [DataMember] or [IgnoreDataMember]. The result: a member T marks [IgnoreMember] is still serialized, [Key(int)] keys become string keys named after the members, and [DataContract] types serialize undeclared public members.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests (IgnoreMemberOnReferencedMessagePackObjectIsHonoured, DataContractOnReferencedTypeIsHonoured). On head the generated formatter still references 'SecretValue', so both fail.

findings.claim: The README says the surrogate 'is only read at compile time and is never instantiated', and its example surrogate has no [MessagePackObject]. The code requires [MessagePackObject] on the surrogate (it reports TypeMustBeMessagePackObject and generates nothing otherwise), requires an accessible parameterless constructor, and instantiates the surrogate at run time through GetSurrogateConversionCode. Copying the documented example therefore gives a compile error and no formatter. The attribute's own XML doc says the opposite of the README.

receipt_plan.detail: Use the GeneratedFormatterForReferencedTypeTests harness. Compile the README surrogate example verbatim: MyObjectSurrogate without [MessagePackObject], plus [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(MyObjectSurrogate))]. Assert that the generator reports no diagnostics and that the formatter has a Serialize member. Expect it to fail on head with MsgPack003 and CS0535.

findings.claim: Contractless mode here covers only public read-write members and a parameterless constructor. Get-only public properties are silently dropped from serialization. Types that have only a parameterized constructor are rejected with NoDeserializingConstructor (constructorParameters is always empty). The existing contractless resolver serializes readable members and matches constructor parameters, so 'contractless behaviour over public members' is only partly delivered for immutable library types.

receipt_plan.detail: Use the generator harness with a ProjectA type `public class P { public P(int id) { Id = id; } public int Id { get; } }` and a bodyless [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] for it. Expect on head: a NoDeserializingConstructor diagnostic and no formatter. Then compare with DynamicContractlessObjectResolver, which round-trips P.

findings.claim: Suppose T is declared in the same compilation with [MessagePackObject] and also has a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] formatter. TypeCollector emits its own formatter for T, and GeneratedFormatterCollector adds a second ObjectSerializationInfo for the same data type. The generated resolver then gets two registrations for T, which is a likely duplicate-key failure or an arbitrary winner. Nothing deduplicates or diagnoses this.

receipt_plan.detail: MessagePackGenerator.cs:60-76 adds the generatedModel to modelPerType unconditionally after Collect(typeSymbol) has already added the [MessagePackObject] model for the same type. Confirm with a test that declares [MessagePackObject] class T plus [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class TF : IMessagePackFormatter<T>, then inspects the generated resolver for two entries for typeof(T).

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Contractless means only public, read-write instance properties and fields, keyed by name as strings, deserialized through an accessible parameterless constructor. CreateContractlessMembers filters on IsPublicReadWrite. Get-only members are skipped, and types with only a parameterized constructor are rejected with NoDeserializingConstructor.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Contractless means the same semantics as the existing DynamicContractlessObjectResolver: every public readable instance member is serialized, including get-only ones. Deserialization matches constructor parameters by name and then sets the writable members. Minimal edit: in CreateContractlessMembers include readable members with IsWritable set from the setter. Fill constructorParameters by choosing the best-matching public constructor instead of passing Array.Empty. Drop the parameterless-constructor check at line 77, or keep it only as a fallback.
